comparator.name: Society, Language and Culture (Samenleving, Taal en Cultuur)
comparator.academicYear: Indicative prospective cohort sequence: year 1 2027–28, year 2 2028–29, year 3 2029–30; checked 2026-09-25
comparator.route: Ordinary non-abroad specialisation with French language-and-culture minors
comparator.sourceNotes: Radboud identifies the target as the named specialisation of Algemene Cultuurwetenschappen (CROHO 56823), not a generic French degree. Official prospective year pages provide 60+60+60=180 EC: year one has 60 EC compulsory language/communication, European/global culture, intercultural study, environmental humanities and methods, with zero-credit mentoring excluded. Year two has 30 EC compulsory material culture, music/social interaction, climate interaction and a partner project, plus two required 15-EC language-and-culture minors chosen in one of three areas (French, German or Spanish). The first listed French package is selected neutrally; its component minors include language acquisition/proficiency, linguistics, literature and culture, which the year page does not itemize into individual credits. The selected ordinary non-abroad third year has 15 EC environmental humanities, 5 EC sustainability whitepaper, a 10-EC individual final work and 30 EC genuine free study/internship space. The alternate abroad third-year route replaces the 15-EC humanities block with 15 EC other-faculty electives alongside 30 EC abroad, and is not combined. The prospective pages for 2027–30 form an indicative entrant-cohort sequence, not adopted OER guarantees.

alternatives.label: Culture, communication and social sustainability
alternatives.concept: A broad UCR response studies culture and its material heritage, language and media, intercultural communication, social relationships, environmental history and climate communication through empirical and humanities methods. It does not provide the 30-EC French language-and-culture sequence chosen in the Radboud comparator.
alternatives.labelReason: The course mix visibly combines cultural study, communication and social sustainability rather than implying French, German or Spanish language proficiency.
progression: Introductory cultural, communication, media, social and sustainability courses precede advanced theory and practical work; prerequisites and term availability are satisfied.

alternatives.label: Environmental culture and sustainability communication
alternatives.concept: This route asks how culture, ethics and communication shape climate response while adding ecology, water, sustainability policy and applied research in a delta. It pursues a stable environmental-humanities direction supported by the programme; UCR’s stronger environmental-science component and missing language minors remain explicit differences from Radboud.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule has sustained climate, ecology, water and governance work as well as cultural and media study, so the label reflects the mixed humanities-and-environment programme.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes II, which precedes Renewable System Design; the other selected courses satisfy their formal prerequisites and scheduled terms.
alternatives.distinctness: The environmental route shifts several courses from general media, world archaeology, literature and art history to ecosystems, water, sustainable design and environmental research, while retaining culture and climate communication as the organising link.

routeSelection.route: Ordinary non-abroad specialisation with French language-and-culture minors
routeSelection.basis: The target itself is the named Society, Language and Culture specialisation. The non-abroad third-year route is the ordinary first-listed route; among equal language-area minors the official page lists French first. This neutral tie-break does not consider UCR course availability. The 30-EC third-year free space remains open.

selection.assessment: A broad cultural-communication programme and an academically distinct environmental-culture direction pass evidence, coherence, distinctness and feasibility. A third language-area direction would require sustained French, German, Spanish or multilingual proficiency and region-specific advanced study absent from the current UCR catalogue; separate language candidates are assessed individually rather than repackaged as a token third alternative.

notes.text: Radboud combines social and environmental sustainability with 30 EC in one chosen French, German or Spanish language-and-culture area and a partner-linked cultural capstone. UCR can build coherent culture, communication and sustainability programmes but does not teach those required foreign-language sequences, so no UCR course or general intercultural study is presented as their equivalent.
